subject.title: Anthropic setup-token onboarding path has multiple failure modes (docs gap, credential propagation, multi-agent sync)

question: Should Anthropic setup-token/manual-token onboarding copy static token profiles into sibling agent stores, or keep current main-store inheritance and focus this issue on setup-token UX plus validation?
rationale: Both directions can fix user pain, but they make different security and upgrade tradeoffs around copying bearer tokens versus relying on inherited runtime resolution.

options.title: Prefer inheritance plus validation
options.body: Keep one canonical/default auth store, improve setup-token instructions, and add explicit status or doctor validation without copying token material by default.

options.title: Approve static-token sibling sync
options.body: Allow setup-token and paste-token paths to copy portable static token profiles into configured sibling agents with focused tests and security-facing docs.

options.title: Close after live no-repro
options.body: If current-main live setup-token proof shows the user path is fully fixed, close this and route only broader auth-sync policy to the related rotation issue.

recommendation.title: Prefer inheritance plus validation
recommendation.body: Keep one canonical/default auth store, improve setup-token instructions, and add explicit status or doctor validation without copying token material by default.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest current history for main-store read-through, secrets startup, and auth storage policy points to steipete for the credential-boundary decision.
